exposure: objectively measured sleep quality (total sleep time, sleep efficiency, wake after sleep onset, sleep onset latency)
outcome: fetal outcomes (premature birth, small for gestational age)
cohort: A total of 1,610 pregnant women aged 18 or older were recruited during early (week 10-14) to mid-pregnancy (week 16-19).
finding: Poor sleep in early to mid-pregnancy was associated with a higher likelihood of emergency caesarean section and an overall trend towards lower levels of inflammatory markers, but no other maternal or fetal outcomes like pre-eclampsia, premature birth, or small for gestational age.
mod_finding: Poor sleep in early to mid-pregnancy was associated with an increased likelihood of requiring an emergency caesarean section.
cross-section timing: Data collection occurred during early (week 10-14) to mid-pregnancy (week 16-19).
